content.thinking:
Since there's no low-poly kit available, I'll plan the elephant model manually: an African bush elephant with roughly 3.2m shoulder height and 3.6m body length, standing in a rest pose with straight column legs, spread ears, a curved trunk, tusks, and a tail.

For the geometry, I'll use faceted sweeps with about 7 sides and flat shading to keep the low-poly aesthetic crisp. For color, I'll mostly rely on flat facet colors but add a subtle paint effect for skin mottling and a dust gradient on the lower legs to give some richness without breaking the low-poly feel, then start laying out the skeleton proportions in meters—shoulder height around 3.2m, back dipping toward a 3.0m rump, and belly height near 1.45m above ground.

Now I'm mapping out the spine joints from hips to shoulders to neck base, placing the head center with a domed forehead reaching about 3.3m, and routing the trunk from the face down to the ground with a curled tip, roughly 2.2m long. I'm also defining the front leg placement and tapering radius from shoulder to foot, planning toenail details and the nearly-straight limb structure typical of an elephant.

The guide calls for separated, extended digits, so I'll give each foot small toe joints—maybe four per foot—mostly tucked inside the rounded column shape of the foot, keeping the toe detail subtle rather than fully splayed out.

For the ears, I'm planning huge Africa-shaped ear shapes around 1.2m tall and 1.1m wide, each driven by a hinge joint at the head so they can flex naturally.

I'll keep the rig simple — a single bevel-extruded ear with inner pink-grey paint and radial vein lines added via a paint function, sitting at roughly a 30° outward spread so the ear partially covers the shoulder behind the head.

Working out the attachment geometry for the ear, I set the outline to hinge at a vertical line along the head's side, shaped like a broad-topped, narrow-tipped leaf, with the extrusion axes angled outward and back so the ear's face normal points forward-out at about a 35-40° splay from the body.

For the trunk, I'm planning a chain of about eight tapered joints swept with an octagonal cross-section, shrinking from a thick base to a narrow tip, with wrinkle detail added either through darker painted ring bands at intervals or through small ridge-like ring sweeps, and considering a rippled radius function as an alternative way to fake the wrinkle texture geometrically.

I'm giving the trunk end two small finger-like lips and a dark nostril disc, letting the trunk hang in a gentle S-curve from the face with the tip lightly curled forward and kept just off the ground, then moving on to shaping the downward-then-forward curving tusks extending from the upper jaw.

Now I'm thinking through the mouth structure: a small lower jaw beneath the overhanging trunk base, built as a capsule shape with a pale lower lip and chin, plus the head itself as a domed cranium with cheeks and forehead lofted along the neck.

For the main body I'll loft it over the spine chain to the neck, with the head as a separate rigid sweep system attached at the head joint. I'm working out the head stations front-to-back—sizing width and height at each cross-section—aiming for a head roughly 1.1m tall and 0.9m wide at the crown, with the convex African elephant forehead domed up near shoulder height.

I'm placing the trunk base emerging from the front of the forehead around [0, 2.25, 2.55], and setting up the head and jaw joints aimed forward. Now I'm laying out the full spine chain from rump through hips, back, withers, and neck up to the head joint, which the body loft will follow.

For the loft, I'm computing width and height profiles at each spine station -- rump, hips, mid-body, chest, and neck -- shaping a belly-heavy silhouette by shifting the center y lower at the belly stations, then checking that the resulting top/bottom extents stay consistent across stations.

Writing bone chain setup...

Working out joint counts and chain structure...

I'm simplifying the neck to a single span, with the head joint placed at the skull base, separate from the lofted body mesh. The pelvis serves as the root joint and the start of the spine chain.

For the tail, I'm planning a 5-joint chain hanging from the rump down toward mid-calf height, tapering thinly and ending in a fan of coarse spike-like hairs, with the rest pose angled slightly back and out rather than straight down.

Now I'm working out the front leg chains, placing hip, elbow, wrist, and ankle/foot joints at specific coordinates so the legs reach naturally down to foot pads near ground level.

Naming the chain joints and tapering the leg radius from thigh to wrist, then adding a separate flat-soled foot pad as its own small lathe shape.

I'm planning the foot structure: a faceted round pad cylinder tapering upward for the elephant foot, with four small toe nails and digit joints positioned around the front rim for subtle toe articulation.

For hind legs, I'm mapping joint positions from hip through knee, hock, and foot, giving the thigh a fleshy, forward-knee elephant shape with bulging mass spheres at the shoulder and thigh to blend the legs into the body, plus a tapering radius profile along the leg sweep and knee wrinkle detailing. I'm settling on a grey-brown skin tone for the palette.

Now I'm building out the full color palette: light and dark skin tones, a dusty reddish-brown for the lower legs and back to mimic dust-bathing, pink ear interiors, ivory tusks with darker tips, pale nails, dark amber-ringed eyes, black eyelash spikes, and a coarse black tail tuft. I'm also sketching a paint function that blends dust coloring near the ground with a mottled two-tone body coat for low-poly patchiness, plus wrinkle shading.

I'm layering thin stripe-based wrinkle lines on top of the mottled coat, then working through texel density math to decide between a 2048 or 4096 texture atlas so the wrinkle bands stay crisp without overkill for a low-poly style — leaning toward 2048 for sufficient detail.

Now I'm designing the ear paint: distinguishing front (exposed, pinkish with radiating veins from the hinge point) versus back (greyer) using the face normal, plus a darker rim along the edge, and computing vein angles radiating outward from the attachment point.

Then I'm working out the eye construction — a dark socket sphere with an amber iris disc, eyebrow ridge, and lash spikes — positioning it laterally on the head between ear and trunk by seating it to the nearest surface point, before moving into the cranium loft stations for the head shape.

Next I'm sketching twin dome bumps on the forehead using two flattened low-poly spheres stuck onto the skull surface near the top front.

For the trunk, I'm chaining it from the head, defining a curved series of points that narrow and droop downward from the face before curling forward and upward at the tip, aiming for roughly a two-meter overall length typical of an elephant trunk.

I'll label this chain segment "tentacle" and taper the trunk radius from 0.30 down to 0.09, adding ring ripples and subtle folds with a lighter underside, using a fractional pattern along the trunk axis to paint periodic rings.

For the trunk tip, I'm shaping a small dorsal spike with a shorter lower lip, and modeling the nostril as a dark flat oval cap at the end with two nostril holes, oriented along the forward-up tangent direction. Now I'm moving to the jaw, placing its joint and lofting it from the mouth area down to the chin.

Tusk sockets emerge symmetrically from the upper jaw flanking the trunk base, with dark pink mouth corners and a lower lip, while the upper jaw/lip mass forms a wide loft connecting into the head around the trunk base and down toward the face front.

Now I'm figuring out the ears, hinging them at points behind and above the head to aim downward and outward. I'm shaping each ear as a large Africa-like lobe, extruding an outline from the attachment point along the back of the head, with the shape flaring outward and down from that vertical attach line.

I'm defining the outline points for the ear, measuring widest spread near the top and the sharp lower tip giving the Africa-like silhouette; the first pass came out too tall at 1.8m against the real ~1.2-1.5m reference, so I'm scaling everything down by about 0.85 to bring the height to roughly 1.4m and width to 0.9m.

For the ear structure, I'm keeping it simple with two hinge joints (root and tip) rather than a full membrane simulation, using a rigid extrude with a small concave notch at the rim edge for character. I'm also planning sparse low-poly bristle spikes scattered on the forehead crown and back, around 0.04m each, rather than detailed hair cards.

For the bristle hair, I'll avoid individual spike parts since hundreds would blow past the 1000-part limit, so instead I'm using flat textured cards — a simple tuft design with three dark strokes, scattered maybe 120 on the head and 60 on the back plus a tail brush, keeping the part count manageable. I'm also noting remaining small details to add: sixteen toenails with toe bumps, eyelashes as a ring of small spikes, and a temporal gland streak marking.

Now I'm planning the temporal gland streak as a small dark brown decal stripe between the eye and ear, plus skin folds — raised wrinkle rings around the knees, ankles, and elbows using closed-loop sweeps with low side counts to keep triangle counts reasonable, roughly three rings per joint across the legs. I'm also starting to think through the tusks as curved sweep shapes.

Checking the triangle budget and setting up a shared low-poly geometry helper with flat shading for faceted surfaces while keeping tube bending smooth.

For legs I'll use fewer sides (8) with faceted normals, and for the body loft I'm leaning toward 10 sides with flat shading for a cleaner barrel shape, versus maybe 6-8 for the trunk with some ripple detail. I'm also double-checking that the body loft's bone chain aligns correctly with the pelvis and spine joints so the mesh starts at the right point along the spine.

I'm mapping the tail's parent to the pelvis, and figuring out which spine segment each pair of legs should attach to -- hind legs to pelvis, front legs to the spine segment near the shoulder height. For the leg sweep, I'm thinking through how the radius function should interpolate along the chain so the taper looks right, and I'm planning to add a separate low-poly cylinder as a foot piece at the tip joint.

Now I'm working out the foot details -- round for front, oval for hind, with a flat sole -- and adding small wedge-shaped toenail boxes positioned radially around the front rim of each foot, aimed outward and spaced across a forward-facing arc.

Still working through the ring geometry...

I should add toe pads using small icosahedron rocks parented to the foot joints, and figure out nail counts biologically accurately—using 4 front toes and 3 hind toes to match real anteater anatomy. Now I'm setting up the skin color palette for the body paint.

I'm building the body texture by layering a mottled base pattern with fold-colored wrinkle stripes, thinking through whether the wrinkle axis should follow a horizontal band around the body or run diagonally along the flanks to mimic real wrinkle patterns.

Now I'm considering generating a separate leg-specific wrinkle ring pattern using the sweep coordinate, and exploring whether a cellular crack pattern would better capture the mosaic texture of elephant skin for the body overall.

Still writing dust blending logic...

Flat colors for tusk, nail, and eye are fine as-is; I'll write helper functions for sweep options and verify SweepOptions supports sides and smooth flags. I'm now sketching extra body masses -- shoulder and thigh bulges built from scaled spheres layered onto the loft, with body width and leg radius tuned so they coincide cleanly at the joints.

Now I'm working out the leg's radius profile, keying smaller values at hip, knee, and ankle to taper the shape naturally across the ~1.8 length, and planning the head region directly through joint coordinates rather than a region helper. Writing import statements...

Setting up metadata and skin color constants, then building the main skeleton — starting with the pelvis joint and spine chain using catmull-spline control points to define the elephant's body curve.

Still defining more joints...

Still plotting trunk curve points...

Total length comes out around 2.5m, which works, with the tip slightly lifted off the ground. Now I'm tapering the trunk radii from thick at the base to narrow at the tip, deciding to skip ripple ring geometry for now and move on to sprouting the tusks from the skull.

For tusks, I'm sweeping a curved path from the lip outward and tapering, going from a thick base radius down to a sharp point, with the total tusk length landing around 1.7 meters.

Adjusting the tusk colour bands with stained base and ivory tip, plus adding subtle growth-ring texture using a paint function tied to a periodic fraction of the surface coordinate. Now I'm figuring out eye placement by computing surface hit points on the skull mesh.

Still defining cranium loft stations...

Now I'm skipping cheek and brow geometry for now, relying on paint detail instead, and working out the ear bone placement and joint origin relative to the skull's side surface so the ear attaches naturally at the back of the head.

Still computing ear orientation...

The outward normal for each face should work fine regardless of mirroring since paint just follows the actual normal direction. I'm now checking the ear's tilt angle—the plane direction suggests the ear extends outward and slightly backward, roughly 29 degrees from the lateral axis, which should position it naturally relative to the head.

Checking the ear's vertical placement: with the joint at y=3.05 and scale factor 0.85, the lowest point lands around y=1.9, which keeps it hanging in front of the shoulder appropriately, and the ear sits outside the body's width at that height, so the geometry checks out.

Now I'm working out ear thickness and bevel values, then thinking through the pink mottled interior paint versus a darker rim band using a normal-direction check to distinguish fold edges from flat surfaces, deciding to skip rim hair detail, and starting to lay out the tail's chain of points curving down and back from the base near the hips.

I'm continuing the tail setup with five segments tapering in radius toward the tip, then designing a spiky tuft ring at the tail's end, using tilted spikes angled to follow the tail's downward direction for a natural tuft look.

Next I'm moving to the body loft stations, sketching out centered cross-sections along the spine from rump to shoulders—adjusting width and height at each point to shape the pelvic crest, hip bump, and rib taper into a believable elephant torso silhouette.

The pelvis bone starts at -0.9 but the loft begins at -1.75, so the first bone takes ownership there. The belly can sag slightly like a real elephant, and I'm checking the body skin smoothing settings before moving into writing the legs build function.

I'm naming the leg joints per side, giving front legs shoulder/elbow/wrist/hand and hind legs hip/knee/ankle/foot, each parented to the spine or pelvis with a "leg" role and contact points.

Now I'm sweeping the leg geometry into a tapered tube with flat caps at the foot, then adding a cylindrical foot pad and a small fetlock bulge near the ankle for shape.

For the toes, I'm placing a ring of digit joints around the foot's tip, spaced by angle with front feet getting four and hind feet three, each named individually and parented to the foot tip. Then I'm attaching small nail boxes embedded into each toe joint to cap them off.

Skipping toe separation lines since the joints already convey that, I decide to add toe pads instead—rounded boxes embedded into the foot front to make each toe read clearly, then placing the nail slightly further out on top of each pad.

For colors, the sole pad stays a darker skin tone while nails get a light ivory-grey shade. Next I'll move on to thinking about body folds, possibly using loops to generate them.

Adding wrinkle loops at joints...

Adding trunk ridge loops along tangent frames at regular intervals, then starting on eye placement by sampling the skull surface for hit points.

Adding eyelash spikes and frame details...

Now for the temporal gland stain, I'll draw a tear-drop drip shape decal placed at the skull hit point, oriented along the surface normal with soft tapering edges. Then for hair, I'm sketching bristle card shapes as angular jagged strands for texture.

Hair placement covers the crown, forehead, back, chin, and trunk base with scattered bristle cards filtered by normal direction and minimum spacing, plus thin wiry cards for a tail tuft. For the mouth, I'm lofting the lower jaw bone through a few width/height stations with a darker lower lip tint and a small dark line marking the mouth corner.

Now I'm adding a dark gum-colored rod along the jaw junction to suggest mouth interior, plus extra chin bristles, a thicker lip/face mass ring at the trunk root with a wider base radius, and starting on the nostril disc at the trunk tip.

For the nostril, I'll make a flat dark disc facing forward at the tip, maybe with a pink inner ring, rather than separate holes. I also need to add the trunk's finger-like projections near the tip—a dorsal spike pointing up-forward and a smaller ventral one—positioned using the sweep's surface angle so they sit correctly on the trunk's upper and lower sides.

I'm deciding to skip genitalia and anus details, but I could add small touches like knee pad bumps, shoulder skin folds, scars, and light mud/dust patches on the ears for texture, plus maybe a few bristle cards just on the tail.

For the trunk, I'm computing fold rings along its length by checking a periodic fraction of the position coordinate to decide where fold color appears versus skin color. For the body I'm layering patch-based coloring with several skin tones plus a dust overlay, and for the legs I'm nesting a ring-band pattern on top of smaller patches so the paint function recursively calls itself for the base layer before applying the ring bands.

Now I'm confirming the paint resolution chain works correctly—outer paint functions set a "current" sample context before resolving nested paints, so inner functions and dust wrappers inherit the right surface sample. I'm checking that chain tube parameterization is keyed to a 0-1 position along its length, noting the ear needs no dust layer, then moving to writing the actual bone and joint setup—ears as hinge joints aimed downward—and placing body parts like spheres using geometry, color, and transform options.

I'm now working out the forehead domes using scaled icosahedron geometry, deciding their color should inherit from the shared coat paint. For the tusk base, I'm planning a short sheath piece using a sliced sub-path of the tusk sweep with constant radius to visually wrap around where the tusk emerges from the skin.

Moving into the actual limb rigging code, I'm defining joint coordinates for hind legs (hip, knee, ankle, foot) and front legs (shoulder, elbow, wrist, hand) as polylines, letting the sweep rounding smooth the corners naturally. I'm also noting the tail chain needs five named points to produce four spans plus a tip joint, and now I'm positioning a foot cylinder at the tip of the hand joint...

Still tuning limb radii...

The shoulder bulge is too much, so I'll shrink the leg radius and bring the leg centers closer together, using around x=0.52 for front legs and 0.55 for hind, with a tapered top radius near 0.40.

Now I'm structuring the toe/joint data, naming each digit joint with its role, and defining how the ring radius extends outward along the centerline for each one. I'll also add dust texture to the skull matching the body paint, then build the tusk path using a Catmull-Rom curve that both the sweep geometry and sheath will reference.

Sheath and tusk sweep geometry, with the sheath sized slightly larger than the tusk base, plus hair cards and remaining wrinkle/fold details on the cheek and trunk base. I'll also add forehead bumps and hind nail counts, then move on to writing it out, typechecking, and previewing.

input.command: mkdir -p scratch/africanElephantSonnet; ls samples | head -5; grep -n "role" src/skeleton.ts | head -20
